set.approach: Park at the Appalachia trailhead on Route 2 west of Gorham and hike up the Airline Trail, then the Randolph Path and finally the Short Line, which delivers you onto the ravine floor; it is a long approach, longer if you are breaking trail, and many side trails cross the area so carry a map. From the foot of Great Gully, look for the curved gully on climbers' right at the far right side of the ravine. A short bushwhack leads into a narrow snow gully, followed by a few hundred feet of snow to the first ice. The ravine is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: From the ridge above, you can walk off by Lowe's Path or ski down one of the ravine's gullies.

review.notes: Approach and line from the Crossbow page; trailhead and trails from the area page. Walk-off from the Crossbow page.

set.approach: Park at the Appalachia trailhead on Route 2 west of Gorham and hike up the Airline Trail, then the Randolph Path and finally the Short Line, which delivers you onto the ravine floor; it is a long approach, longer if you are breaking trail, and many side trails cross the area so carry a map. From the ravine floor follow the Great Gully trail, if you can find it under the snow, to the foot of the gully, which is hard to miss. Expect to push through brush at the bottom when the snow is thin. The ravine is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Any of the trails down to Appalachia works (Airline, Valley Way or Spur Trail). In good conditions, walking around the lip of the ravine and down the Airline gives a view of the route.

review.notes: Route page for the line and descent; area page for trailhead, trails and the list of descent trails.

set.approach: Park at the Appalachia trailhead on Route 2 west of Gorham and hike up the Airline Trail, then the Randolph Path and finally the Short Line, which delivers you onto the ravine floor; it is a long approach, longer if you are breaking trail, and many side trails cross the area so carry a map. Follow the same line as for Great Gully, then branch to climbers' left at the obvious gully with ice steps. If you cannot see well, the right gully is the second one to the left of Great Gully, not the one next to it. The ravine is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Link up with the hiking trails (Airline, Valley Way or Spur Trail) to return to Appalachia.

review.notes: Route page for the approach and the link-up with trails; area page agrees on the trail descent.

set.approach: Park at the Appalachia trailhead on Route 2 west of Gorham and hike up the Airline Trail, then the Randolph Path and finally the Short Line, which delivers you onto the ravine floor; it is a long approach, longer if you are breaking trail, and many side trails cross the area so carry a map. The Short Line takes you to the south wall; the route is the second ice and snow gully on the right. A boulder field with some bushwhacking lies below it. The ravine is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Parties can rappel the route, or top out and walk down one of the ravine's descent trails (Airline, Valley Way or Spur Trail). The exit can go left, which is easier, or right over thin ice and mixed ground below a steep triangular rock face. Dense spruce below the exit is the worst of it whichever way you go.

review.notes: Route page: location on the south wall, exits, spruce hazard and descent suggestion; area page: trails and descent trails.

set.approach: Park at the Appalachia trailhead on Route 2 west of Gorham and hike up the Airline Trail, then the Randolph Path and finally the Short Line, which delivers you onto the ravine floor; it is a long approach, longer if you are breaking trail, and many side trails cross the area so carry a map. Follow the line of the summer route and bear right where you can, staying near the small band of cliffs that marks this part of the headwall. The route starts at the obvious slab of water ice. The ravine is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Descend the summer trail on the same line, which brings you back to the ice slab; the gully forks near the top and either branch is fine. The ravine's other trails down to Appalachia are the alternative.

review.notes: Route page; area page for trailhead, trails and descent trail names.

set.approach: Park in the Willey House lot on Route 302, cross the Saco River on the bridge and head north up the notch to the slabs. The couloir is the northernmost of the four prominent gullies seen from the road, just before the Webster Slabs. Trend up the right margin of the slabs to its base. The slopes above can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page; area page for the Route 302 / Saco River crossing.

set.approach: Use the pullout on the east side of Route 302 nearest the Willey's Slide parking, cross the Saco River and head south over a rocky debris field. It splits into two fields that quickly rejoin; follow the gully uphill to the Gallery area. This line is the one first seen on your right as you arrive. The slopes above can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Approach from the route page; no descent stated anywhere.

set.approach: Start on the Central Couloir approach from the Route 302 parking by the Saco River bridge, then break right at the headwall. Green Chasm is the first gully to the right of Central Couloir. The slopes above can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route page for position relative to Central Couloir; Central Couloir page for the shared start. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the base of Green Chasm, traverse right (south), passing the two VO2 gullies, until you reach this route. The slopes above can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Single route page; no descent stated (page warns against bushwhacking from the top).

set.approach: Park on Route 302 as for Shoestring Gully, cross the Saco River and follow the trail left for a few hundred feet, then turn right into the woods toward the gully, which is very prominent from the road and lies just north of Shoestring. A large talus field right of its base is a useful landmark. The slopes above can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: When the ice ends you can bushwhack straight through the trees to the Webster Cliff Trail, then turn right (south) and follow it down to Route 302.

review.notes: Route page; descent via the Webster Cliff Trail also stated on the Shoestring Gully and Landslide Gully pages.

set.approach: Park in the Willey House site lot on Route 302 and cross the Saco River on the bridge beside it. The gully is the prominent one directly across the river, south of Central Couloir. The slopes above can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Turn right (south) onto the Webster Cliff Trail and follow it down to Route 302, then return to your car by the road or the trail beside the Saco River. That trail is very steep, so crampons may be useful.

review.notes: Route page for approach and descent; Shoestring Gully page confirms the Webster Cliff Trail descent.

set.approach: Start from the Webster Cliff trailhead and use that trail's bridge over the Saco River. Just above the bridge a blue-blazed trail joins from the left; turn left along it to a large boulder marked with blue arrows. There, leave the trail on a diagonal to the right and follow the climbers' path (or flagging) into the gully. Snow or rock leads up for several hundred vertical feet to the first ice. This is the southernmost gully on the mountain. The slopes above can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: From the top, walk straight up into the woods for a few minutes to meet the Webster Cliff Trail, then turn right (south) and follow it out to the road. It is one of the steepest trails in the range, so crampons may be needed.

review.notes: Route page for approach and descent; Landslide and Horseshoe pages agree on the Webster Cliff Trail descent.

set.approach: The gully is at the far north end of the Webster slabs, reached by a long, steep snow slope. Locate the gap in the trees beneath the gully, then work up the snow slope to the foot of the ice. The slopes above can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Parties can rappel the route or descend to the left. Do not try to bushwhack up to the Webster Cliff Trail.

review.notes: Single route page; descent options as the page gives them.

set.approach: Use the pullout on the east side of Route 302 nearest the Willey's Slide parking, cross the Saco River and head south over a rocky debris field that splits into two fields and quickly rejoins. Follow the gully uphill to the Gallery area; the route starts where the Gallery Route curtain ends on the left. The slopes above can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Approach from the route page; no descent stated.

nh_4_mt_webster_winter_ice_mixed_unknown.skip_reason: page gives only the buttress it sits on, no approach, and its descent remarks are about a fixed anchor of uncertain existence

set.approach: This remote north-facing area is reached from the Lincoln Woods parking lot: cross the Kancamagus Highway and head straight into the woods on snowshoes, over open, easy snow bushwhacking, to the frozen cascades. Expect a long day in and out.

review.notes: Area and route pages agree on the approach; route-level GPS is inconsistent so no distance given. No descent stated.

set.approach: This remote north-facing area is reached from the Lincoln Woods parking lot: cross the Kancamagus Highway and head straight into the woods on snowshoes, over open, easy snow bushwhacking, to the frozen cascades. Expect a long day in and out. The route sits right beside the neighbouring flow but the two do not join.

review.notes: Area and route pages agree on the approach. No descent stated.

set.approach: From the Crawford House lot, walk the railroad tracks past Mt. Willard, then climb the Mt. Tom snowfield slopes, keeping to the left side of the higher slopes. Go a long way up, then head left into the woods to find the ice curtain. Expect deep, post-holing snow. The slopes above can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.

review.notes: Route and area pages agree on the tracks and snowfield approach; area page admits uncertain location. No descent stated.

set.approach: Hike in on the Sawyer Pond road and the popular Signal Ridge route, then continue to Carrigain Notch; snowshoes are needed once you leave the packed Signal Ridge trail. The gully is on the south side of the notch, on your right as you approach. Leave the trail at the notch and bushwhack through the woods to its base. It is a long day.
set.descent_text: From the top you can walk the ridge south and rejoin the trail, or visit the nearby summit first. Parties also rappel and downclimb the gully, using a large tree at the top and smaller trees partway down.

review.notes: Approach and descent from both pages; they give different descents so both are offered.

set.approach: The route is on the central south side of the notch. Park at the pull-off directly below the climb (coming from Errol, the second pull-out on the left, just before the height of land), though the climb may not be visible from the car. The base is reached by a direct climb up the steep hillside. The slopes above can slide, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: Walk down to the west, or rappel from trees. A walk-off trail sits well back from the top and can be hard to find, and a long rope may not reach the ground from the anchors, so be ready to build a thread.

review.notes: Route page; area page confirms it is on the notch.

set.approach: Winter access is by ski or snowshoe. From the Lincoln Woods lot on the Kancamagus Highway, a long ski leads to Thirteen Falls Campground; turn left onto the Franconia Brook Trail, do not cross the brook, and follow an old logging road through short pines to the crag, which is hard to spot in deep snow. Shorter options: follow the Garfield Trail to the Appalachian Trail and drop toward Thirteen Falls before traversing the slope until the crag appears, or take the Gale Head Trail to the hut and head south. The area is protected wilderness, so place no permanent anchors. The route is the narrow runnel just east of the Descent Route.

review.notes: Area page approach; route page location and descent.
